name: zlib-d
algorithm: Decompress a zlib stream (RFC 1950) made once by Go's compress/zlib at level 6 with each language's library, checking the Adler-32 trailer, reading the input and writing the output file in 64 KiB chunks; the check is the output file's SHA-256 (README.md).

c.name: zlib
c.inside: none (the portable C of adler32.c, crc32.c, deflate.c, trees.c, zutil.c and the inflate files; no assembly, no intrinsics)

rust.name: flate2
rust.inside: its default rust_backend: miniz_oxide 0.8.8 and adler2 2.0.0, which forbid unsafe code; crc32fast 1.4.2, linked, has unsafe SIMD (pclmulqdq) for gzip's CRC-32, which the zlib framing does not run; flate2's own unsafe code is in its C backends, not enabled

notes: The input is tools/bench gen kind zlib of words (seed 3, bytes 200,000,000: whole words up to that size, then a newline) compressed once by Go's compress/zlib at level 6; every cell reads the same compressed bytes. The size is provisional: verify -publish-size in the coordinator's window fixes it.

Every cell checks the trailer's Adler-32: inside the library for C (zlib), Rust (miniz_oxide), Go and Mk; the Zig program computes it with std's own hasher, because Zig 0.17's Decompress reads the trailer without comparing it (BS-1). Every cell also checks the header's FCHECK and refuses FDICT (RFC 1950 2.3); the Zig program checks those two bytes itself, because Decompress checks CM and CINFO only.
C: zlib 1.3.1 from Mk-evidence/vendor (D-588), compiled with the C column's flags. Rust: flate2 1.1.1 from a cargo vendor tree in Mk-evidence (crates), by directory source replacement (D-835).
